I'm going to go straight off the bat and say Dunkirk is one of the weakest Christopher Nolan films I've seen. I saw this in 70mm IMAX, which greatly added to the immersion of being on Dunkirk beach, with the dog fighting in particular being very enjoyable. But its greatest feature, immersion, is its only feature. A lackluster story and dialog leaves the film feeling like a collection of war porn cut in the Nolan style . Whilst 'show, don't tell' is a good methodology, its completely overdone to the point that the almost lack of spoken dialog left me not knowing half the names of the characters by the end.

I fell like the movie should of taken a slightly larger view, with more plot points leading upto the beach, to alivate the repetitive nature. by the time the 4th sinking ship scene plays out, your just left wondering - is this it?

The zimmer soundtrack injects tension right into you, especially with the use of shepard tones, and helps captivate the scene to the point your out of breath at the end. Unlike his previous works, I doubt the soundtrack will be enjoyable outside the context of the film, which may or may not be to zimmers credit.

Unlike most war films the rose tinted glasses are left firmly off, to the point I'm surprised it was PG-13. The horrors of war are on full display and uncut. For historical accuracy, it plays it very safe - there are arn't even any Germans in the film.

The good:

  • Cinematography
  • Action Scenes
  • Music

The bad:

  • The abysmal character development (it's WW2 not expecting much)
  • The small choice of plot points to show.
  • Repeating the same set pieces.
